one_month_reasoning: In the window: Q3 2026 results on Oct 29 before the open (consensus Q3 EPS $1.37, Jefferies $1.39), where management said it would roll forward the five-year capital and financing plan and the 2027-2031 outlook, and normally gives 2027 guidance (consensus FY2027 $4.54). Also in the window: the MN gas rate decision (Nov 2026) and the Minneapolis data-centre moratorium review (by Nov 21). What I expect: a bigger capital plan (the $10B+ line-of-sight) is likely, but so is a 2027 guide range whose midpoint sits near or a little below consensus because of the Minnesota base-rate freeze and Colorado's $157M of $356M outcome. Enki notes no new commercial data-centre deals in Q2-Q3 against a target of ~1 GW signed in 2026, so the ESA update is a two-sided risk. Polymarket prices 96.8% for no Fed cut in 2026, so there is no rate tailwind. Net: a slight positive drift (median $77.0, +0.4%, partly the post-selloff bounce) with event-widened monthly vol of ~5.8% vs 5.4% normal (19%/3.5), so the spread is close to symmetric.

fair_value.method: Blend of a P/E leg on a rate-base EPS build (NTM EPS at the horizon $4.79 x 17.5x = $83.6, weight 0.8) and a driver FCFF DCF (WACC 6.4%, g 3.5%, $59.2, weight 0.2 from the 16.9x forward-P/E band). Engine base horizon value $78.71.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCFF FY2026-30 from revenue +6.5%/+9%/+8.5%/+6.5%/+5.5%, EBIT (pretax+interest) 26.4%->31.1%, tax 0%, D&A ~20-21%, capex 80%->51% then 37.5% normalised; WACC 6.4%; Gordon g 3.5%; net debt at horizon $48.3B; 648M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: us-gaap:RegulatedAndUnregulatedOperatingRevenue FY2025 from the 10-K XBRL (the fact pack lacks a revenue tag; read from data.sec.gov companyfacts, accession 0000072903-26-000009).

Non-fuel revenue requirement tracks rate base (~11% CAGR), fuel/purchased power (~35-40% of revenue) is pass-through and flat; FY2026 $15,622M vs consensus $15,606M; FY2027 $17,028M vs consensus $17,150M (-0.7%).

EBIT_t = pretax_t + interest_t, with pretax = NI/1.10 (TTM tax is a net benefit: -$231M on $2,002M pretax, F74/F81) and interest $1.80B, $2.10B, $2.45B, $2.75B, $3.00B (TTM $1,642M, F67, growing with debt). 2026: 2,318+1,800 = 4,118 / 15,622 = 26.4%; 2030: 3,464+3,000 = 6,464 / 20,758 = 31.1%. Not GAAP operating income (F6 $2,789M TTM) because AFUDC-equity and other income are part of regulated earnings.
Reported income tax has been a net benefit three years running (-$146M, -$402M, -$245M; TTM -$231M) as PTC/ITC transfers exceed tax; 0% is a conservative proxy for cash taxes over the plan.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At a 10% tax rate the DCF falls ~$7/share.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2025 D&A $2,968M = 20.2% of revenue; 2026 guidance +$140-150M; grows with rate base.

Capex = change in rate base + D&A: 2026 ~$12.5B (TTM $12,463M, F53); 2027 $11B+$3.4B = $14.2B; 2028 $9B+$3.75B = $12.6B; 2029 $6B+$4.05B = $10.0B. FY2030 is set to the steady-state level for the Gordon terminal: D&A $4.35B + 3.5% x $98B = $7.8B (37.5%), not the plan's ~$10B, so the terminal FCFF matches the terminal growth.

Cost of equity 8.2% = 10y UST 4.9% (Sep-2026 monthly avg 4.99%) + beta 0.6 x ERP 5.5%; pre-tax debt 5.4% (2026 issues 4.15%-5.875%) x (1-21%) = 4.27%; market weights E $47.9B (624.6M x $76.68) / D $39.5B = 55/45. Polymarket prices 96.8% for no Fed cut in 2026, so no rate relief assumed.
Rate-base growth continues after 2030 at ~3.5% (replacement capex, load growth from data centres and electrification) but well below the 11% plan CAGR.
Jul-2026 to Oct-2027: capex ~$17.9B (H2-26 $6.5B + 0.8 x 2027 $14.2B) - CFO ~$7.1B (TTM $4,771M rising) + dividends ~$1.9B - equity issued ~$1.8B (forward settlements) = +$10.9B on $37.4B.

bear.story: Regulation and wildfire: the MN freeze and Colorado historical test years push earned ROE ~30bp lower, the Texas AG Smokehouse case goes badly, data-centre ESAs slip as local moratoria spread (Minneapolis, Eagan, Inver Grove Heights, Rosemount, Carver), and the 10-year stays near 5%. EPS ~4% below the build, group P/E ~15x, DCF at a higher WACC.

base.story: Rate base grows from $66B to ~$77B by end-2027 under the $60B plan plus part of the line-of-sight capital; earned ROE ~8.75%; ~3%/yr dilution; FY2027 EPS $4.44 and FY2028 $4.88; the stock keeps a ~7% P/E discount to peers at 17.5x.

bull.story: The Q3 roll-forward adds $10B+ (2027-31 rate base CAGR ~13%), 1 GW+ of new ESAs (including SPS Panhandle load from AI campuses), Colorado passes wildfire-liability protection, and rates ease. EPS +3% vs the build, P/E 19x, and the discount to peers closes.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount is one I expect to last through the horizon, for reasons in the filings and rate orders rather than sell-side calls: (1) wildfire liability is still open, with Smokehouse Creek at $460M accrued and no upper bound estimable (deck), a pending Texas AG suit, and Colorado still without a liability statute (Jefferies names it a 2027 focus); (2) PSCo, 43% of rate base, earns 7.22% against an allowed 9.3%, and its latest order granted 44% of the request on a historical test year; (3) Minnesota is proposing a base-rate freeze for 2027-28. Against that, XEL's EPS growth (+10% consensus FY2027) is above the peer median of 8.1%, so I do not use the ES-style 13.7x. A move to the median needs a Colorado wildfire statute or a cleaner CO/MN regulatory outcome; that is the bull case.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$64 (about 7% under the 52-week low of $68.72, and ~15x my FY2027 EPS) the market would be pricing a fundamental break rather than rates: an uninsured wildfire liability well above the $525M of cover, a Texas AG judgment that blocks cost recovery, a cut to the equity plan or guidance (EPS growth below 6%), or a large-load tariff or ESA failure that strands capex on shareholders. Normal rate-driven volatility (19% annualised) rarely takes a regulated utility 17% below fair value without one of these.

reverse_dcf_check: The engine says the 17.5x P/E leg implies a 6.0% WACC against my 6.4%. With debt at 4.27% after tax and 45% weight, that is a cost of equity of about 7.4%, 0.8pt under my CAPM figure with a 4.9% 10-year. Put another way, the multiple assumes EPS growth of ~8-9% to 2030 (rate base ~11-13% less ~3% dilution and lag) and then ~3.5-4% for good, an earned ROE that stays above the cost of equity (book ROE ~10.5%), and no permanent wildfire impairment. That is plausible: the data-centre ESAs (2 GW signed or under construction, 15-year terms) and the 20+ GW pipeline back post-2030 growth. The long-dated risks above (about -$3.4/share probability-weighted) are why I use 17.5x rather than the 18.85x median.

sbc_treatment.note: SBC $46M FY2025 (F36), 0.3% of revenue, is expensed in GAAP and ongoing EPS; no add-back. The share count grows ~3%/yr from the equity plan, which is separate from SBC. Peers' consensus is on the same operating-EPS basis.

reasoning: Start: $76.68, down 5.5% over a year and 9% under the February high, after a fall tied to wildfire litigation (Smokehouse Creek, Texas AG), BofA cutting to $80 and Jefferies to $99 on Minnesota/Colorado regulatory risk, Minnesota's Oct 9 base-rate freeze proposal, and a 10-year that rose from 4.1% to ~5%. The build: rate base $56B (2025) to $66B, $77B, $86B, then $92B and $98B including part of the line-of-sight capital; 53% equity; earned ROE calibrated to 8.75% (2026 guidance midpoint $4.10). The opco ROEs explain the discount: PSCo earns 7.2% and NSPM 9.6%. Less holdco interest and ~3%/yr dilution gives EPS $4.44 (2027) and $4.88 (2028), 2% below consensus because of CO/MN lag. Valuation: 17.5x NTM EPS of $4.79 = $83.6, weight 0.8 (the peer median is 18.85x; I keep a ~7% discount). The FCFF DCF gives $59.2, weight 0.2; it sits below because the regulated return barely beats a 6.4% WACC at today's rates. Blend: $78.7 (+2.6%, plus a ~3.1% dividend). Alternative-lane signals: (a) local data-centre opposition is real and growing (Data Center Watch: ~$198B blocked or delayed in H1 2026; moratoria in Minneapolis and several metro suburbs; Slashdot readers focus on bills and water), which slows approvals but has not touched the signed Google ESA; (b) Enki saw no new XEL data-centre deals in Q2-Q3 2026, so the 1 GW-in-2026 target is a risk for the Oct 29 call; (c) Polymarket gives 96.8% to no 2026 Fed cut, so I assume no relief from rates; (d) Simply Wall St's community narrative value (~$87.5) and TIKR's mean target (~$89.5) sit above me, and SWS's own DCF ($65.7) sits below, which brackets my two legs. Anthropic/WSJ: I found no named Anthropic ESA with Xcel. The one indirect link is the Fluidstack Abernathy TX campus (168 MW, SPS territory per Compute Atlas; Measured AI lists it among Anthropic-linked sites, but Compute Atlas does not confirm the tenant), so I treat it as a low-confidence general demand signal. Anthropic's ~$450B of compute commitments (WSJ) supports SPP/ERCOT large-load demand. Its S-1 risk factor on organised resistance confirms the approval risk I already see in Minnesota. AI-tenant counterparty risk falls mostly on tariff collateral and minimum bills (MN: 15-year minimum, 80% exit charge; CO proposed: 6-month deposit, 80% minimum bill, exit fee = remaining minimum bills); stranded capex built before tariffs or ESAs are in force would fall on shareholders or ratepayers. On Kilian's liquidity-drain question: an IPO-driven sale of liquid defensives could push XEL down for a few weeks, but nothing in the article changes XEL's earnings. A dip toward $70-72 (~16x NTM, 9-11% under my fair value) would be a reasonable add if Q3 guidance holds and nothing new on wildfire breaks; below $64 is the thesis break. Ladder: a mixture of lognormals around the engine's scenarios ($62.4/$78.7/$92.7 at 25/50/25, 12% within-scenario vol) with slightly fatter tails for wildfire and regulatory jumps; P(>=77) is 0.53. Research limits: Reddit, Axios and X were blocked or returned nothing useful; Kalshi snapshots were stale.

model_inputs.dcf_check: DCF $59 vs P/E leg $84 (-29%). The FCFF DCF values the regulated asset base at a 6.4% WACC: EV at the horizon ~1.1x rate base, because the after-tax regulated return (~6.5-6.8%) barely exceeds the WACC and the 2026-28 capex wave ($12-14B/yr) earns its return only with lag. The market prices XEL (and peers) at ~1.3x EV/rate base: the reverse DCF says the P/E leg implies a 6.0% WACC, i.e. a cost of equity ~7.4% with the same debt cost, lower than my 8.2% with a 5% 10-year yield. Kept at the 0.2 weight from the forward-P/E band (16.9x) and not zeroed: it is the honest asset-value anchor and the downside if utility multiples de-rate toward book-plus-growth.
